scope: Source acquisition identity verification before an acquired PDF can be recorded as inspected evidence or projected into Zotero.
observed_failure: During the first collision-review reduction, an arXiv PDF URL returned a valid but unrelated paper. URL success, PDF readability, and a content digest would all have passed the existing provenance checks, so the wrong work could have been recorded as FULLTEXT_INSPECTED under the intended source ID.
counterevidence: DOI-resolved and publisher-hosted files often carry reliable embedded metadata, while scanned PDFs may lack machine-readable titles and therefore require a manual identity decision rather than automatic rejection.
Matching only a normalized title can still accept a preprint or revision different from the cited version.
proposed_mechanism: Before setting FULLTEXT_INSPECTED, compare the intended source identity against at least two available signals among canonical DOI/arXiv ID, landing-page title, embedded PDF title/authors, and first-page title. Record IDENTITY_VERIFIED, IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS, or IDENTITY_MISMATCH separately from download and inspection state; quarantine mismatches and never attach them to the intended Zotero item.

domain_boundary.why_not_domain_specific: A readable but misidentified file can corrupt evidence in every research domain; arXiv merely supplied the observed acquisition route.

evaluation.sample: The next ten newly acquired scholarly PDFs across at least three program directions, including one DOI route and one repository route.
route_level_metrics: number of mismatched or ambiguous files prevented from becoming FULLTEXT_INSPECTED
number of correct files unnecessarily delayed for manual identity review
time added before an honest ATTACH, REINSPECT, or ACCESS_REQUIRED decision
evaluation.rollback_rule: Remove automatic rejection and retain only an identity-warning state if the check falsely rejects two correctly identified files or cannot produce a reviewable reason for a mismatch.

does_not_establish: Identity agreement does not establish cited-version equivalence, lawful redistributability, inspection quality, comprehension, claim support, novelty, or a lifecycle transition.
